transcript: The death of someone you love is not a wound that simply heals. It is a landscape you slowly learn to walk in. You suffer because you keep searching for them in the place they used to stand. But love does not disappear when a body does. You are not weak for feeling shattered. You are witnessing how deeply you were capable of loving. Do not fight your grief. A mountain does not fight the wind. It allows the storm to pass through it. Place your hand on your chest. Feel your heartbeat. That rhythm carries everything they ever gave you. Nothing real is lost. They are no longer here to be held. But what they planted in you still breathes. Your task is not to move on. It is to become strong enough to carry both the sorrow and the love at the same time. Walk forward slowly. Breathe slowly. Let the way you live be the monument you build in their honour. And when the weight feels unbearable, return to your breath. You are not alone in this darkness. Stay steady. The light returns quietly. If you need a quiet place to return to, I have created one. The Inner Circle. Private teachings. Daily guidance. No pressure. Three days free. The link is in my profile.
